objective: Proof: for G~ = GL(2,3) or the binary octahedral group, central extensions of S4 by Z/2, every homomorphism from a knot group to S4 lifts to exactly two homomorphisms to G~ (the lifting obstruction lies in H^2 of the knot group, which vanishes, and the lifts form a torsor for H^1 = Z/2), so the maps sending meridians to lifts of transpositions number 2T(K) and are #P-hard to count; the unrestricted count |Hom(knot group, S4)| = 4 + R + 2T, with R the 3-cycle colourings (polynomial through A4) and the 4-cycle colourings equal to T (Livingston 1995), so unrestricted counting is #P-hard for S4, GL(2,3) and the binary octahedral group on knots. The closed-manifold version for the double covers is recorded as open: the naive surgery identity fails. Standard-library checks.
status: Proved by SL23-BOUNDED-20261025-001B-P001: every map from a knot group to S4 lifts to exactly two maps to GL(2,3) or the binary octahedral group (H^2 of a knot group vanishes), and |Hom(knot group, S4)| = 4 + R + 2T with R the 3-cycle colourings (polynomial) and the 4-cycle colourings equal to T (Livingston 1995); so counting maps from knot groups to S4, GL(2,3) or 2O is #P-hard with or without the meridian condition. The closed-manifold version for the double covers is open: the naive identity 8 + 2T for p = 4 surgery fails on some knots.
title: The double covers of S4 are #P-hard on knots
